publicReleaseNotes:
Nook 0.3.0 adds visible decision and request history, live thread reply counts, clearer invitations and channel access wording, and shared Notified names and urgent reasons. Phone composition stays above the tabs. History and Decisions & requests controls reference panels only while mounted; member erasure waits for the refreshed people list before its receipt returns focus to the surviving page.

Nook now pins the published rer 0.2.19 command line. A fresh local launch creates a placeholder owner; choosing a real local owner is optional and keeps the owner ID and data. Setup applies pending migrations during local updates. A hosted deploy claims the owner after health succeeds and removes its one-time setup token; rer signin provides single-use owner access with the deployment's own Cloudflare credentials. Local archive restore instructions recover the archived identities before setup.

Imported-reaction erasure continues in bounded steps until the erased Slack ID is absent, rather than completing with a retained ID. Migration 0024_import_redaction_steps.sql adds the resumable import/redaction state; 0025_owner_signin.sql adds hashed one-time owner sign-in grants. Both migrations are additive. Export before updating from 0.2.0, keep private settings and all applied migrations unchanged, then run rer setup locally or rer deploy against the existing hosted installation. Never reset populated state to update.

Known Base issues remain: invitation links expire after 15 minutes (invite the person again); the hosted Lobby can ask for a setup token after owner claim (open /signin); and rer 0.2.19 removal can fail with provider-incomplete-pagination on a nonempty R2 bucket (empty only that deployment's bucket and rerun removal). Reply counts include live replies only; Open thread still reaches erased-reply tombstones. Real-device Web Push receipt and virus scanning are not claimed.

NOOK-009.summary: Document both the offline filesystem-operator backup and the active hosted owner-session export, with restore remaining local.
NOOK-009.was: Full backup was described only as an offline filesystem-operator capability that bypasses app privacy; ordinary app-admin export was excluded.
NOOK-009.now: Offline local backup and hosted export through an active owner session both write verified archives and the erasure journal. Hosted import is not authorized; restore remains offline into an empty local destination. Sessions, sign-in tokens and outbox mail are excluded.

NOOK-013.summary: Make notified names, the urgent marker and urgent reasons visible to all current channel members.
NOOK-013.was: The clause specified recipient validation and attention routing but did not state whether members who were not notified could see notification metadata.
NOOK-013.now: All current channel members can see the message’s Notified names, Urgent marker and urgent reason, including members who were not notified. Attention routing and recipient validation retain their existing rules.

proseChanges.summary: Describe the 0.3.0 local and hosted owner journeys, safe updates, and offline identity recovery after restore.
proseChanges.was: First setup required an explicit local owner, hosted setup described a manual setup-token claim, and archive import did not link the exact offline identity-recovery procedure.
proseChanges.now: A fresh local launch creates a placeholder owner and optional setup keeps its ID and data. Hosted deploy claims the owner and removes the setup token; rer signin provides mail-free owner access. Local updates stop dev and apply pending migrations with setup. Restore links to offline identity recovery before setup; the 0.2.0 upgrade lists migrations 0024 and 0025.

proseChanges.summary: Run the exact package-mode rer dependency and treat local owner setup as optional.
proseChanges.was: The guide ran the published rer package through a shorter first-run journey without describing the placeholder owner or the checkout-managed Node and pnpm versions.
proseChanges.now: rer runs the exact pinned devDependency with the declared Node and pnpm versions; dev prepares a placeholder local owner and optional setup replaces its email while keeping the owner ID and data.

proseChanges.summary: Specify the proven local restore and hosted owner-claim procedures and bound prior-format recovery claims.
proseChanges.was: Restore referred to general identity mapping, hosted owner claim required manual bootstrap, and the legacy recovery wording did not distinguish the supported backup-only portability-v1 path.
proseChanges.now: Local restore recovers explicit archived identities offline before setup at the original D1 binding path. Deploy claims the hosted owner and removes the setup token. Backup-only portability-v1 recovery verifies checksums and records the unverified-metadata acknowledgement; older document formats remain separate offline procedures.

migrations.buyerSteps: Apply with rer setup locally or rer deploy against the existing hosted database. Adds import-kit preparation/stream-source tables and resumable reaction-redaction progress for pending member erasure. No manual data conversion or reset is needed.

Apply with rer setup locally or rer deploy against the existing hosted database. Adds hashed, expiring, single-use owner sign-in grants for rer signin. It creates no sign-in grant or notification merely by being applied.

agentUpdateInstructions: Updating from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0: preserve the existing owner, data, private settings, resource identities and every applied migration byte. Stop local dev and export a private backup first (rer export locally, or rer export --target remote through the active hosted owner session). Fast-forward the checkout to the 0.3.0 source. rer manages the pinned dependency graph and tooling; run rer setup then rer dev locally, or rer deploy with the existing Cloudflare account and environment for a hosted Nook. The only new migrations are 0024_import_redaction_steps.sql and 0025_owner_signin.sql, both additive; never reset populated state to update. Existing email and push choices stay unchanged. The next hosted deploy claims an unclaimed 0.2.0 owner and removes its unused setup token; an old .rer/deploy/production-secrets.json can then be deleted. Restoring an archive is a separate empty-target operation: follow OPERATIONS.md#restoring-a-local-archive and recover the archived identities offline before setup. Keep the documented Lobby, invitation-lifetime and R2-removal limitations visible until their Base fixes ship.
